scope.candidate_feedback: GMST-triggered Amazon forest dieback CO2 emissions recursively passed into FaIR
excluded: Amazon rainfall recycling and regional hydrology damages
a scalar uplift applied to an existing SCC

give_audit.finding: FaIR has a temperature-dependent land-uptake term but no explicit Amazon carbon stock, dieback state, or Amazon emissions input

unit_contract.temperature_input: annual global-mean temperature anomaly in degC on the calibration baseline
unit_contract.fair_conversion: divide GtCO2 by 3.6666666667 for GtC per year if target FaIR E_co2 uses GtC per year
unit_contract.causal_lag: temperature through year t generates Amazon emissions entering the CO2 cycle in year t+1

forbidden_claims: Amazon dieback adds a fixed percentage to the GIVE SCC
the combined EPA permafrost and Amazon uplift identifies either component
META's 0.1 percent SCC increment transfers to GIVE
FaIR temperature-dependent uptake either fully includes or fully excludes all Amazon climate-carbon feedback
the GMST-only hazard captures precipitation, drought, fire, and deforestation interactions
unlock_requirements: Verify scenario-by-scenario whether GIVE baseline fossil and land-use emissions contain Amazon dieback responses
Quantify and remove overlap between the added stock-release process and FaIR's temperature-dependent land uptake
Update or bound the hazard using current evidence that Amazon response depends on precipitation, drought, CO2 fertilization, land use, and fire as well as GMST
Condition the stochastic state on observations through the pulse year and document the temperature baseline
Replace the release rule with an exactly stock-conserving final installment for noninteger duration draws
Implement the one-year-lagged recursion in baseline and pulse models with identical hazard uniforms and parameter draws
Run zero-feedback, zero-pulse, pre-pulse identity, pulse-size convergence, mass-balance, and time-step tests
Validate temperature and emissions paths against META and at least one independent process-based or Earth-system benchmark
